PolitiFact's fact-check was published 2020-03-02, after the 2020-02-19 runtime reference date, though it uses data contemporaneous with the debate (the $64.2B Forbes estimate was current around Feb. 2020).
The 'bottom 125 million' figure derives from an estimated household-to-person conversion (2.63 members per household), so it is approximate (~125.7 million).
Net worth for the bottom percentiles can be negative, per caveats critics raised at the time, though the retrieved records include no refuting evidence.

Bruenig's figure of $11.4B for the bottom 38% differs from Gross's replicated figure of ~$6B, but both are far below Bloomberg's $64.2B, so this numerical discrepancy is resolved and does not undermine the verdict.
